items.followUp: Explain the formation of a coordinate covalent bond in the hydronium ion, H₃O⁺.

rubric.why: The defining feature is that a shared electron pair in a covalent bond is supplied by one atom only.
rubric.how: Award 2 marks for stating that a shared pair in a covalent bond is donated by one atom.

rubric.why: The donating atom provides the bonding pair from a lone pair.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that the donor has or supplies a lone pair.

rubric.why: The other atom or ion accepts the donated pair; in the example, H⁺ accepts it.
rubric.description: Explains the role of the electron-pair acceptor.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying the accepting atom or ion, or stating that it accepts the pair.

rubric.why: Ammonia donates its lone pair to H⁺, forming NH₄⁺.
rubric.description: Gives a correct example of coordinate bond formation.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for giving the formation of NH₄⁺ from NH₃ and H⁺.

modelAnswer: A coordinate covalent bond is a covalent bond in which the shared pair of electrons is donated by one atom only.
The donating atom has a lone pair, while the other atom or ion accepts that pair.
For example, nitrogen in NH₃ donates its lone pair to H⁺ to form NH₄⁺.
The bond may be represented by an arrow from the donor atom to the acceptor: N→H.
